title: With Eyes Full of Affection
lead: In the analysis of the song, it is important to note the poetic tadbhava forms (hiyá instead of hṛdaya, mukutá instead of muktā) and the blend of awe and fear with tenderness toward the Unknown Traveler.

words.meaning_here: in the eyes, in the gaze
heartfelt attachment, tenderness, sense of kinship
words.note: Literally “the feeling that something is one's own, dear”.

lines.structure: Modifier of the subject “traveler” (line 2): adverbial of place (নয়নে) + qualitative modifier (মমতা ভরা).
lines.literal: In the eyes with tenderness full,

words.note: মুকুতা is a poetic tadbhava form of Sanskrit muktā (pearl).

heard: In the word mukutájhará, the singer clearly articulates an open syllable and pause: mukutá jhará
The verb tharathara is drawn out and separated as tharo tharo
interpretation: The song conveys the experience of the sudden appearance of the Supreme Beloved (Parama Puruśa) in the form of an Unknown Traveler (Ajáná pathik). His gaze is filled with unconditional maternal care and love (mamatá), and His smile sheds a radiance of purity (mukutá jhará). The encounter with the Infinite awakens in the devotee's heart a tremor of sacred awe and shyness (láje bhaye), in which the mind dares not look directly, yet becomes saturated with the deepest nectar of divine sweetness.
